title: Added latency exposes unmatched-leg losses in the frozen risk gate
research_question: Does the frozen risk gate retain downside performance when submission is delayed, and where do its losses occur?
hypothesis: The earlier fresh-seed and adversarial results would remain competitive after added submission latency.
interpretation: The gate downside score changes from +0.497 at baseline to -0.643 with 200ms additional submission latency. All six losing delay variants contain residual executed leg shares, across five source groups in volatile/disappearing families. Their combined loss is 21.928 virtual USD; baseline has five losing variants across four groups with combined loss 11.258. These accounting components describe the observed losses without proving causation.
caveats: Synthetic economic coefficients are not observed fees or calibrated execution.
All four conditions reuse the same 100 groups; 6000 variants are correlated, not 6000 independent samples.
Training support uses feature ranges, not joint-distribution or probability calibration. Fee changes may force abstention because the model was trained at zero synthetic fees.
Different actions and latency alter execution noise; common seeds do not guarantee common fills.
Post-evaluation descriptive analysis; no model selection or retuning
Binary settled positions only; proportional per-asset cash-flow allocation includes fill fees
Residual shares describe executed legs before settlement, not remaining terminal inventory
Execution variants are correlated within source groups; no independent-sample inference
Attribution is accounting decomposition, not causal identification or an executable recovery policy
Synthetic hypothetical outcomes; no empirical fill calibration or real profitability claim
Fee-coefficient condition abstains on unsupported inputs; zero is not evidence of profitable fee robustness.
Half-depth condition changes capacity and decisions; it is not an isolated sizing experiment.
next_experiment: Keep these failures as saved-action accounting regressions; preregister fresh latency/family challenges before evaluating revised policies. Do not tune on these opened cases.
